title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
summary: ‘It’s only been done once and that’s what we want’ Arteta not being drawn on City’s financial charges Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the ­target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season. Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches. Continue reading...

title: French and Bulgarian presidents condemn violence at Marseille v Levski Europa League game
summary: Emmanuel Macron: incidents had ‘no place in sport’ Nazi salutes alleged among Levski Sofia fans The presidents of France and Bulgaria have condemned violence that broke out at a Europa League fixture between Marseille and Levski Sofia in the Stade Vélodrome. Television footage showed Marseille fans cornering a group of Levski supporters in the stands before beating them relentlessly, including with a belt. One Levski fan is seen bleeding from the head as he receives multiple blows while trying to protect a female friend. Reports from inside the stadium on Thursday suggested violence began after a Levski supporter was seen making a Nazi salute. Continue reading...

title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
summary: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer. On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

title: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
summary: Club activate option and plan further talks with captain ‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes. Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers. Continue reading...

title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
summary: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters followed a four-letter suggestion to tell the defender: “You’re not welcome here.” Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted for the first of his two goals. The result, coming after Forest’s win against Manchester City in their last match at the City Ground, means they climb three points clear of the Premier League’s relegation zone. Continue reading...

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. title: Football Daily | Watford, the Pozzos and the hottest managerial seat in the game
summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! A few weeks ago, Alessio Dionisi was forced to deny the “fake news” he had joined Sean Dyche, Gianfranco Zola, Beppe Sannino, Óscar García, Billy McKinlay, Slavisa Jokanovic, Quique Sánchez Flores (twice), Walter Mazzarri, Marco Silva, Javi Gracia (twice), Nigel Pearson, Vladimir Ivic, Xisco Muñoz, Claudio Ranieri, Roy Hodgson, Rob Edwards, Slaven Bilic, Chris Wilder, Valérien Ismael, Tom Cleverley, Paulo Pezzolano and Edward Still in being sacked by the Pozzo family since 2012. There was no denial on Sunday, when the axe inevitably fell on the head coach following a 4-0 shellacking at Sheffield United and the Italian left after only 18 games in charge. While his reign is unlikely to live long in the memory of anyone at Vicarage Road, Dionisi can at least boast on his LinkedIn page that in terms of longevity under the Pozzos, he took charge of 18 more matches than Dyche, 17 more than García and 16 more than McKinlay. Indeed, he even outlasted Rob Edwards, who was assured he would be backed “come hell or high water” upon his 2022 appointment, only to be fired from the ejector seat 11 games later. title: Why have things started to go wrong for Manchester City under Enzo Maresca?
summary: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling . Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. City have appealed against the ruling, saying they are “innocent of the accusations”. Continue reading...

title: All Blacks have ‘no gas in the tank’ but stats show it’s England who should be out of juice
summary: Figures indicate England’s players have far more rugby miles in their legs than Saturday’s opponents but Borthwick has managed to balance heavy schedule The prevailing narrative emerging before England’s rematch with New Zealand on Saturday is that the All Blacks are running on fumes. The forwards coach, Jason Ryan, has said that “there is not much juice in the tank” while Graham Henry, who led them to the 2011 World Cup title, has continued the theme in even starker terms. “It’s the end of the season and we’re buggered. They’ve just got no gas in the tank.” It is understood that narrative has raised a number of eyebrows within the England camp. The view, as England seek to clinch a third straight win over New Zealand for the first time in the history of the fixture, is best summed up as, “welcome to our world”. We are nearing the end of a gruelling year for the All Blacks, who give the impression they cannot wait for their season to end, but the grind in England, that which led to Maro Itoje being ordered to take the summer off, is at the very least comparable. title: England target historic All Blacks treble after finally clicking into gear
summary: Maro Itoje says the team have used morale-sapping defeats this year to reach this stage but there is ‘more to come’ Offer England’s players a choice between a cut-price “Black Friday” deal and another super soaraway All Black Saturday and this week’s answer is unanimous. This may be an opportune moment to snap up pre-Christmas bargains on the high street but Maro Itoje and his side are rather more intent on securing a priceless little chunk of history. Never before in 121 years have England’s men beaten New Zealand in three consecutive Tests and the last time their opponents lost six times in a calendar year was back in 1949. During that distant annus horribilis the All Blacks ended up contesting simultaneous Test series against South Africa and Australia and lost them both; this time around there would be no such asterisk. Hamilton and Leclerc clashed on track at the last round in Las Vegas, only two weeks after similarly contesting a place in Mexico cost them a potential one-two. title: Finals weekend will show who really holds rugby power heading into World Cup year | Ugo Monye

It has been 12 months of either feast or famine, of boom or bust. The worst ever Six Nations performance followed by another fine autumn as they head into Saturday’s rematch with the All Blacks. Their lowest ebb under Steve Borthwick in Rome and their best performance last weekend since he took charge. Without getting ahead of ourselves, the next Six Nations has taken on a very different complexion after this month’s results and performances. There is a big, humble reminder given that England enjoyed a clean sweep last autumn and then endured such a disappointing Six Nations, but there is a different feel about them 12 months on. Despite the winning run that England were on, there was still grumbling about their playing style. That is no longer the case. title: McNabney’s late double powers Ireland to dominant win against Australia
summary: 3rd v 3rd: Ireland 38-14 Australia Henshaw, Timoney and Baloucoune also scored tries Ireland’s class told in the end. Back-to-back victories to end the year would have been a tonic for a much-criticised Wallabies team and while they started strongly, they were ultimately outclassed. Australia have now lost seven matches in a row against Ireland. There was a time not so long ago when such a statistic would have been unimaginable: it is one of many that demonstrates how Australia have declined as a global force. Sam Prendergast kicked brilliantly, off the tee and from hand, to orchestrate a success that was a classic Irish blend of power and finesse. The Ireland fly-half kicked five conversions and a penalty for 13 points and his tactical kicking was world class, too. Two victories against the Wallabies have been achieved in the Nations Championship, and this was more convincing than the 33-31 ten-try thriller in Sydney in July. Continue reading...

title: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished. But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

title: Nigel Starmer-Smith obituary
summary: England rugby union player who became one of the best-loved commentators in the game over a 42-year broadcasting career Nigel Starmer-Smith was an England rugby scrum-half whose international debut at Twickenham, five days before his 25th birthday on Christmas Day in 1969, was a historic first ever win for England over South Africa. But it was as a broadcaster that he was best known. After his playing career ended he became a schoolteacher, then made a move to the BBC where in the 1980s he fronted Rugby Special, a Sunday TV highlights programme, which gave the then-amateur sport of rugby union a wide national audience. The undisputed voice of rugby was the lilting Scottish brogue of Bill McLaren , but Starmer-Smith, who has died aged 81, became the voice of the English shires. In his clipped, professional tones, he would tell his post-prandial Sunday audience the news from the muddy touchlines of places then familiar on the English rugby map: Bedford, Coventry, Otley, Redruth. Change was in the air, but rugby union was some years from its professional revolution in 1995 and, in England at least, Starmer-Smith represented a now lost cosy world of mud, fellowship and beer. Yet on a muggy Friday night on Vulture Street, the locals had precious little material to work with and the traditional script was flipped on its head.
